A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreeScale and retain matching methods and experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices, including rendered equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SDXL image and VideoCrafter2 video experiments, component ablations, qualitative demonstrations and a 23-user image preference study.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds super-resolution comparisons, video preferences, additional image metrics and further application demonstrations.

M1.justification: V1 uses semantic masks to control regional detail weights. V2 additionally injects region-specific text conditioning through cross-attention for local semantic editing (Section 4.1, Figure 5). The three central pipeline components remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds a local semantic-editing task involving hair and face edits. LAION-Aesthetics-V2-6.5plus and WebVid-10M coverage remains unchanged; rectangular generation and FLUX-assisted enhancement already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds SDXL+Real-ESRGAN as an evaluated super-resolution comparator (Appendix B.1, Table 4 and Figure 8). The original image and video comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: V2 adds Inception Score, video preference evaluation for text alignment, cover quality and video quality, additional aspect-ratio settings including quantitative evaluation at 2048×4096, and SDXL-Turbo demonstrations with two and four steps. The original caption counts and SDXL/VideoCrafter2 sampling defaults are retained.

E4.justification: The existing image and video component ablations remain, with Inception Score added to image ablations. V2 adds targeted case studies of semantic editing, SDXL-Turbo compatibility and contrasting SDXL/FLUX resolution failures (Figures 5, 11 and 13).

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and preference percentages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The added video preference results continue this reporting practice.

E6.justification: All previously tabulated benchmark, ablation and image-study values are retained. Substantial additions include IS results, super-resolution and 2048×4096 comparisons, and video preferences: FreeScale receives 64.62% for video quality (Table 6). New editing, fast-generation and failure examples, plus revised gallery outputs, broaden the qualitative evidence.

T1.justification: The diffusion, cascade, detail weighting, dilated convolution, attention and fusion mathematics in Equations 1–7 is unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs or theoretical guarantees are added or revised.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the first-8k-generation claim to text-to-image generation without additional pose constraints, acknowledging BeyondScene. Its conclusion also explicitly highlights local-control flexibility. The central tuning-free scale-fusion contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets mixed super-resolution comparison outcomes through task differences and specifies UNet repetition versus DiT blur. It states a 512-multiple resolution constraint, but removes v1's warning about quality loss when passing FLUX-generated images to FreeScale.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies the resolution-dependent Gaussian-blur kernel size and standard deviation of 1. V2 also completes the reported video resolution from '640' to '640×1024'. These clarify documentation; the existing sampling settings, hardware and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused references, notably BeyondScene to qualify 8k novelty and I-MAX to contextualize the DiT limitation, alongside references supporting new metrics, models and resolution methods. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 expands cascade and local-control explanations, moves dataset descriptions into Appendix A, reorganizes supplementary evaluations and applications, and makes limited language and author-header corrections.

P2.justification: V2 adds figures for editing, super-resolution, aspect ratios, SDXL-Turbo and architectural failures, plus three comparison tables. Existing image tables gain IS columns, Figure 2 labels skipped steps, the 8k gallery is revised, and several existing displays are relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful validation through super-resolution comparisons, video preferences and IS results, qualifies the novelty claim, and improves reproducibility through Gaussian-filter settings. These are incremental gains. The video study does not clearly report its own sample count, and removing the FLUX-handoff quality-loss caveat slightly weakens the limitations discussion.
